name: Sushi Roll Land - All You Can Eat
notes: Own site (Next.js, server-rendered HTML - dish data embedded directly in DOM, not client-fetched). A la carte menu extracted from raw HTML by matching each dish card's div boundary directly (not text-flattening, which corrupted names by merging adjacent cards) - name from the roll-specific <h4>, price from the primary price <span>, In/Out ingredients captured as description where present. Verified every section's extracted count against the site's own per-section '<N> items' badge count and all 21 food sections matched exactly (APPETIZERS 24, SHOOTERS 3, SALAD 5, BENTO SPECIALS 1, SPECIALTY BOWLS 5, FRIED RICE 4, SIDE ORDERS 3, YAKISOBA 5, RAMEN AND UDON 6, CARPACCIO 7, SUSHI 26, SASHIMI 8, SASHIMI BOWLS 3, CUT ROLLS 14, HAND ROLL 15, NO RICE ROLLS 9, TEMPURA ROLLS 8, BAKED ROLLS 4, SPECIAL ROLLS 25, COMBINATION SET 6, DESSERTS 3 = 184 items). An earlier extraction pass mistakenly captured a per-section 'Extra Sauces' condiment-upcharge widget heading as if it were a roll name (borrowing a neighboring roll's price); the corrected card-boundary-based extraction does not exhibit this bug (checked - zero 'extra sauce'/'add item' matches in final output). DRINK MENU section (53 items, nested sub-categories like BEVERAGE/DRAFT BEER/etc.) renders behind collapsed accordions with prices not present in the fetched static HTML - excluded as adjunct rather than guessed. Also added the site's published All-You-Can-Eat pricing (Adult $39.99 / Kid $11.99, the restaurant's stated core dining format alongside a la carte) as two additional entries under an 'All You Can Eat' section, taken verbatim from the homepage pricing block ('Pricing: Adult: $39.99 Kid: $11.99'). Note: batch-listed website is sushirollland-sd.com (a separate, newer Next.js domain) but sushirollland.com's own JSON-LD confirms the identical address (3955 Fifth Ave, San Diego, CA 92103) and the same restaurant, so the source used is confirmed correct for this location.

The /menu landing page is a shell linking to the real server-rendered menu page (/menus/menu?location=vista), which carries a full schema.org JSON-LD graph including a Menu entity with hasMenuSection->hasMenuItem->offers.price. Address in the JSON-LD (2205 S Melrose Dr #103, Vista, CA 92081) matches the batch address exactly, confirming correct location. 57 of 77 raw menu items had a structured offers.price; the remaining 20 (all Deli Classic sandwiches plus two Bear Favorites subs) had no offers field but their description text stated real 'Chilled $X.XX | Grilled $Y.YY' variant prices, so each was split into two priced dish entries (e.g. 'Deli Classic Ham Sandwich (Chilled)' / '(Grilled)') using the two distinct prices actually printed, not an average or guess. name: Tacos El Franc
notes: Own site (tacoselfranc.com, Otter/'tryotter.com'-powered ordering pages) - the root location page (/gaslamp-quarter) initially 403'd a bare curl but returned 200 with a full desktop-Chrome User-Agent; the location-specific menu subpage (/menu/gaslamp-quarter) needed the same UA plus sec-fetch-* headers and a same-origin referer to get past a 403. Confirmed address '528 Fifth Ave' / '92101' present in the page, matching the batch address. The rendered HTML shows only 8 'Most ordered' carousel items with prices; the FULL priced catalog (45 items across 9 categories) is embedded as an HTML-entity-escaped JSON blob inside an inline <script> tag (a client-hydration payload, keys like allergens/amount/derivedPrice/description/id/name per item, plus a separate 'categories' array mapping category name to a list of item ids). Naive nearest-neighbor text-proximity matching of item name to price was tried first and produced clearly wrong/shuffled pairings (caught via a sanity check against the rendered-HTML carousel prices, which didn't match); the reliable extraction instead brace-depth-parses each self-contained item object (which carries its OWN name+derivedPrice+id together) and separately parses the 'categories' array to map each item's id to its true category name, avoiding the mismatch. One item (VEGGIE MULITA) is cross-listed in two categories (Mulitas and Vegetarian) in the source data; only one instance was kept since it is the same dish. 'hasVariablePricing:true' items (the Beef Tallow Fries family and Veggie Fries) are marked with a trailing '+' to indicate a starting/base price with modifier upcharges possible, per the standard convention used elsewhere in this batch - not fabricated, this is the base price from the data itself. Cent distribution (.25 x9, .50 x8, .75 x12, .95 x11, .45 x2, .65 x2) is entirely conventional/charm pricing with nothing scattered, consistent with genuine own-site pricing - filed high confidence as this is the restaurant's own ordering platform.
